dns.action: Increase replicas to 3 and enable geo‑distributed DNS caching
dns.reason: Utilization is 200% with critical status, causing high latency for name resolution

app-server.action: Add 30 more stateless app server instances and enable auto‑scaling based on CPU/QPS
app-server.reason: Current utilization is at capacity (100%) and status is critical, leading to request queuing

cache.action: Cluster Redis (sharding) into 3 nodes with read replicas
cache.reason: Cache utilization 200% and critical status create cache misses and increased DB load

rate-limiter.action: Scale rate‑limiter to 3 replicas and partition limits per user segment
rate-limiter.reason: Utilization 125% indicates throttling bottleneck, risking denial of service

message-queue.action: Deploy a multi‑node queue cluster (e.g., Kafka) with replication factor 3
message-queue.reason: Queue utilization at 100% and critical status may cause message loss or back‑pressure

architectureChanges: Introduce a CDN edge cache before DNS to offload static asset requests
Add a dedicated read‑replica layer for NoSQL DB to serve read‑heavy URL lookups
Move heavy write operations to an asynchronous worker pool via the message queue
Implement circuit breaker between API Gateway and App Server to isolate failures
Enable global load balancer with geo‑routing to route users to nearest DNS/Cache cluster

connections.reason: Place CDN in front of DNS to serve static redirects and reduce DNS query load
Direct traffic from CDN to LB for efficient request distribution
Standard entry point; ensure LB health checks include new DNS replicas
Rate limiter should be upstream to protect downstream services
Scale rate limiter to prevent it becoming a choke point
Clustered Redis will distribute cache load and reduce hot‑spot
Add read‑replica DB nodes for URL lookup queries
Queue cluster ensures reliable async processing of analytics and logging
Export queue metrics to monitoring for proactive scaling

summary: The current design shows five critical bottlenecks: DNS, App Server, Cache, Rate Limiter, and Message Queue. Scaling out these components, clustering the cache, and moving to a multi‑node queue will immediately relieve pressure. Adding a CDN edge cache, read‑replica DB, and global load balancer improves latency and resilience.
